module.basics.description.text:
The starting point, learn all the basics of the language.

Declaring variables, calling functions, and all the things you need to know before moving to the next lessons.

module.concurrency.description.text:
Go provides concurrency features as part of the core language.

This module goes over goroutines and channels, and how they are used to implement different concurrency patterns.

module.generics.description.text: Learn how to use type parameters in Go functions and structs.

module.methods.description.text: Learn how to define methods on types, how to declare interfaces, and how to put everything together.

site.architecture_languages.text: The server, templates, CSS, JavaScript, images, and fonts are shared where practical. Each language independently maintains course translations, UI text, terminology, and state. Simplified Chinese is the first delivered language, with room for more.

site.architecture_playground.text: Go examples in the browser run through a controlled remote Playground proxy; production does not expose the local /socket code-execution endpoint.

site.architecture_upstream.text: The project continuously records the official upstream commit, preserving a traceable baseline for future source updates.

site.continue_learning_description.text: A Tour of Go is only the beginning. After completing it, visit go.dev for official documentation, tutorials, the standard library reference, the language specification, and more Go learning resources.

site.development_log.text: Development log: A Tour of Go Multilingual Translation Project

site.how_it_works_intro.text: Course localisation is not sentence-by-sentence replacement. It is a workflow built around complete content units, traceable review states, and verifiable release artifacts.

site.intro.text: A community-maintained translation project for official Go learning content. Simplified Chinese is the first available language, and the structure can grow to support more languages and Go content.

site.no_affiliation.text: This project is not affiliated with, authorised by, or endorsed by the Go project.

site.operations_note.text: This site may display advertising to help cover infrastructure costs such as servers, bandwidth, and CDN services, as well as the ongoing cost of maintaining the project. The source code remains public, and self-hosted deployments do not enable this site's advertising configuration by default.

site.title.text: A Tour of Go Multilingual Translation Project

site.tour_description.text: An interactive introduction to the Go programming language.

site.translation_validation_intro.text: The project keeps the learning experience close to the official source while checking every release before publication.

site.unofficial.text: Maintained by Yongye · Unofficial community multilingual translation project

site.validation_examples.text: Go examples with translatable natural-language comments also enter the unified validation workflow; all other examples continue to use the official source directly.

site.validation_page_unit.text: Translations use complete course pages as their unit.

site.validation_present.text: Each release is parsed with present.

site.validation_render.text: Rendered pages are checked before release.

site.validation_structure.text: The page structure is compared with the official source.

site.workflow_process.text: Each unit moves through translation, automatic validation, Translation Quality Review, promotion, ready, projection, and publish; generated translations are never published directly.

site.workflow_publish.text: Publishing builds a complete localised projection from canonical ready candidates, requires every workflow TranslationUnit to be ready, then creates the production binary, release.json, and SHA256SUMS and verifies the complete bundle.

site.workflow_review.text: Automatic checks protect structure, parse present content, compare it with the official source, validate rendering and pages, and check Example Go content. An independent translation quality review is still required before promotion.

site.workflow_units.text: TranslationUnit represents both complete Pages and eligible Examples: a Page is a complete present.Section, while an Example is a complete .go file containing translatable natural-language comments.
